hero.heading: Shroom and Gloom Achievements Guide
hero.lead: Shroom and Gloom ships with 14 Steam achievements. This page lists every achievement name from Steam, fills in publicly visible descriptions, and flags hidden text or patch repairs so you do not chase a broken objective.

sections.heading: Achievement Summary
paragraphs: Steam lists exactly 14 achievements for Shroom and Gloom. Some descriptions are public on the global stats page. Others appear blank until you unlock them in-game. Official patch 0.6.24 specifically called out repairs for “Gloom Slayer” and “Would you love me if I were a worm.”
Use this page as a checklist. When Steam still hides a description, the table marks it as hidden rather than guessing a condition.

sections.heading: Before You Start
paragraphs: Update Shroom and Gloom through Steam before chasing rare achievements. Launch-week patches repaired at least two achievement triggers, so an outdated client can waste a clean run.
Open Steam’s achievement panel and this checklist side by side. Public descriptions here match Steam’s public text; hidden rows are intentionally incomplete.
Decide whether you are hunting mapping goals, collection goals, or combat milestones. That choice changes which path and quests you should prioritize first.
bullets: Install the latest Steam build before retrying repaired achievements
Treat hidden Steam rows as unknown, not as community spoilers
Use Forgotten Path mapping runs for Spelunker-related progress
Keep a simple note of which achievements already popped on your profile

sections.heading: Easy-to-Miss Achievements
paragraphs: Spelunker is easy to miss if you race for bosses and never finish mapping. Its public description requires mapping every tunnel of The Forgotten Path. That overlaps with exploration quest goals discussed on the quests and Concerned Parent pages.

Collector requires 100 different cards, so narrow drafting can delay it. Heavy Handed needs a 20-card hand, which usually means building draw and hand-size effects on purpose rather than playing every card immediately.

Would you love me if I were a worm? is publicly described as killing 10 worms. If it failed to pop before patch 0.6.24, update the game and continue worm kills rather than assuming you are on the wrong objective.

paragraphs: Official Steam patch notes for 0.6.24 state that achievement “Gloom Slayer” should work now and achievement “Would you love me if I were a worm” should work now. If the expected action completed before that patch and nothing unlocked, update and retry.
Hidden rows stay marked hidden. Reviewed on 2026-09-17 against Steam achievement stats and official patch notes.

sections.heading: If an Achievement Does Not Pop
paragraphs: First confirm the public requirement, if Steam shows one. For worm kills or campfire setup, finish the action again after updating rather than restarting your whole profile.
Second, restart the client and re-check Steam Cloud sync. Early Access can delay the Steam overlay popup even when the unlock already registered.

Third, compare nearby systems. Spelunker tracks Forgotten Path mapping, while quests may track the same exploration with a different hand-in. An achievement popup is not automatic proof that a quest completed.
If the achievement was named in official patch 0.6.24 as repaired, prioritize updating over inventing a new condition.

paragraphs: Achievements are separate from quest unlocks, but the same run actions can advance both. Mapping Forgotten Path helps Spelunker and can also move exploration quests tracked on the quests page.
For character unlock questions, use the characters hub or the Concerned Parent guide instead of treating an achievement popup as a full unlock guide.

hero.heading: How to Unlock Concerned Parent in Shroom and Gloom
hero.lead: Concerned Parent is a launch-roster character built around emotion, card draw, and mood tools. Official materials present the character as unlockable. Exact quest mapping below includes player-reported details and is labeled so you can tell official facts from community reports.

sections.heading: Direct Answer
paragraphs: Official status: Concerned Parent is one of the five Early Access launch characters named by Team Lazerbeam, and developer diary footage describes the character as unlockable rather than the default first pick.

Player-reported unlock path (reviewed 2026-09-17, not an official patch note): many players and independent Early Access databases connect character unlocks to quests such as Search Party, which asks you to discover all tunnels in The Forgotten Path. That objective lines up with the public Spelunker achievement text (“Map every tunnel of The Forgotten Path”).

Because Steam discussions also include threads about Concerned Parent failing to unlock, treat the mapping requirement as the best current community lead, then verify in your own quest log after updating the game.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
paragraphs: Play on the current Early Access build after installing the newest Steam update. Launch-week unlock bugs were actively discussed by players, and official patches in the first week focused on stability and achievement repairs.
Be ready to spend runs on Forgotten Path mapping instead of only boss rushing. If your quest log shows an exploration quest tied to discovering tunnels, prioritize unexplored branches and dead ends.

Official materials say advanced characters and Facility access come from the quest system. You should expect Concerned Parent to appear through that meta progression rather than through a store purchase.
bullets: Update Steam to the latest Shroom and Gloom build
Open the in-game quest log before assuming the unlock is broken
Plan at least one Forgotten Path mapping-focused run
Do not rely on outdated demo assumptions

steps.description: Check the character select screen. If Concerned Parent is available, you are done. If it is locked, continue.

steps.description: Official launch notes say quests unlock advanced characters. Look for exploration or character unlock quests before inventing a new route.

steps.description: Community databases describe Search Party as “Discover all tunnels in the Forgotten Path” with a new character reward. Map every tunnel rather than only the shortest boss line.

steps.description: Launch materials highlight autosave after fights or escapes. Avoid force-closing during unlock hand-in moments.

steps.heading: Recheck character select
steps.description: After the quest completes, return to character select and confirm Concerned Parent is playable.

sections.heading: What Concerned Parent Plays Like
paragraphs: Official developer diary coverage describes Concerned Parent as an emotion- and draw-focused character searching for a missing child. Starting tools highlighted in that diary include Parental Instinct, which creates Hysterical Strength, a temporary mood that adds rage damage to attacks and grows as you draw cards.

The same official overview calls out card-draw tools and attacks that care about attacks in hand, such as Mama Bear and Dad Reflexes. That means the character rewards draw engines and hand density more than slow single-hit setups.
Use the characters page for roster context, then return here when you only need the unlock path.

sections.heading: Why the Unlock Might Fail
paragraphs: Player-reported: Steam discussion threads mention Concerned Parent staying locked after some runs. Incomplete quest progress is the first thing to check before assuming a client fault.

If the quest shows complete but the character stays locked, update to the latest patch, restart Steam, and re-open character select. Official patch notes have not published a dedicated Concerned Parent unlock hotfix line item as of 2026-09-17.
Spelunker and the unlock quest can progress together, but one completing does not automatically prove the other finished.

sections.heading: How to Confirm Success
paragraphs: Success means Concerned Parent is selectable on the character screen and can start a run. A one-time popup or quest completion banner is helpful, but character select is the ground truth.
After unlocking, play one short run to confirm starting cards and Foresight behavior match the emotion/draw kit described in official diary material.

sections.heading: Version and Patch Notes
paragraphs: Reviewed on 2026-09-17. Official sources confirm the character exists in the launch roster and is framed as unlockable. Community sources currently point at full Forgotten Path tunnel discovery as the practical unlock route.
If a future official patch or FAQ publishes exact Concerned Parent requirements, that official text should replace the player-reported section on this page.

sections.heading: Which Character Should You Try First?
paragraphs: If you are still learning the double-deck loop, start with Paperboy on Forgotten Path. Official marketing and diary material teach the early route through that setup.
If you already understand food engines and want cooking synergies, Lunchlady is the cleaner next step based on official diary focus.
If you specifically want Facility systems, wait until that pathway is unlocked and then try Janitor. Official 0.6.39 notes say Facility and Janitor felt too complex for many new players at launch.
If Concerned Parent is still locked, finish the unlock guide first rather than forcing a partial kit comparison on this page.

sections.heading: Unlock Requirements
paragraphs: Official Early Access messaging is clear on the system and less granular on every objective: quests unlock advanced characters and pathway access. You progress the world by completing quests across runs rather than buying characters.

Player-reported (reviewed 2026-09-17): independent Early Access databases list quests such as Search Party (discover all Forgotten Path tunnels) and Want Some More (defeat Megashroom) as new-character rewards. Those rows are useful leads, but this page does not hard-map every reward to a specific character without stronger confirmation.
If you need one concrete unlock path today, use the Concerned Parent page. For pathway unlock talk, use the paths and quests pages.

sections.heading: Future Characters and What Not to Assume
paragraphs: Official Early Access plans mention additional character classes during the EA period. Fan databases may already list names that are not part of the current five-character launch roster. This page sticks to the official five until Team Lazerbeam or Steam news confirms more.
Do not assume demo characters, unused datamined names, or joke entries are currently playable.

sections.heading: Related Systems
paragraphs: Characters change how both decks start, but pathway card pools still matter. A Facility run with Janitor is a different drafting environment from a Forgotten Path run with Paperboy or Concerned Parent.
Achievements can overlap with character goals, especially exploration achievements such as Spelunker, but achievements alone are not a full unlock guide.

hero.heading: Shroom and Gloom Quests Guide
hero.lead: Quests are the official Early Access unlock backbone for advanced characters, pathway access, and broader card pools. This page explains the system with official framing first, then lists community-reported quest objectives with clear labels.

sections.heading: How Quests Work
paragraphs: Official Early Access launch notes say you unlock advanced characters and access to The Facility through quests. The same materials describe quests as the way the strange world grows as you venture deeper.
That means quests are account- or profile-level meta goals, not just one-run side objectives. Completing them changes what you can select in future runs.

Official store FAQ language also says the EA build includes multiple quests, synergies, and unlocks for replayability. Exact live quest text can change with patches, so always trust the in-game log over an older screenshot.

sections.heading: How to Track Quest Progress
paragraphs: Open the in-game quest log before and after each meaningful run. Official materials frame quests as meta progression, so progress should persist across runs once the client saves.

Separate three fields in your notes: the objective text, the reward type, and any assumed character mapping. Only the first two should be treated as actionable until the third is confirmed in your build.
When an objective mentions discovering tunnels, cards, or bosses, check the matching systems the same night: map completion, collection counters, and pathway unlock flags.
bullets: Screenshot or copy the live quest wording if it differs from any guide
Record whether the reward is labeled card pack, new character, or new path
Do not equate an achievement popup with quest hand-in
Re-open character select and pathway select after a completion banner

sections.heading: What to Check Before Repeating a Run
paragraphs: Confirm the quest is still incomplete. Repeating a finished objective will not create a second unlock.
Confirm the pathway required by the objective is the one you are loading. Forgotten Path mapping goals will not advance while you only play Facility.
Confirm your build is updated. Early Access patches can change onboarding and card behavior around Facility content, which affects how efficiently you can finish some objectives.
If your goal is a character unlock, keep the Concerned Parent page open as a companion checklist rather than expanding that whole route inside the quests hub.

hero.heading: Shroom and Gloom Best Cards and Combos
hero.lead: “Best cards” in Shroom and Gloom depends on pathway, character, and whether a card helps the combat deck, the explore deck, or a growth engine. This page teaches evaluation criteria and official combo themes without inventing unverified damage numbers or copying rival wikis.

sections.heading: How to Judge the Best Cards
paragraphs: Official store copy emphasizes two decks, infinite growth/modification, and food-based recovery. A card is “best” when it advances one of those pillars without wrecking the other deck’s tempo.

Score combat cards on consistency, scaling potential, and food or resource generation. Score explore cards on routing power, upgrade access, healing, and whether they set up the next fight. Score camp or modify tools on whether they create repeatable mega-combos.

Because Early Access balance changes quickly, a card that was strong on launch weekend may be patched a few days later. Official 0.6.39 notes adjusted multiple Facility cards and systems, which is a reminder to re-check text in your build.

subsections.heading: Combat finishers and scalers
paragraphs: Look for attacks that grow, gain rage, or improve when you draw or eat. Official Concerned Parent examples include Parental Instinct into Hysterical Strength, then draw payoffs and hand-size attacks such as Mama Bear. Those are official illustrations of the rage/draw mega-combo fantasy, not a universal tier list.

subsections.heading: Food and recovery engines
paragraphs: Official store text makes eating and soup cooking a central combat idea. Cards or camp tools that create reliable food, improve roasted enemies, or convert kills into healing often outperform raw shield equivalents.

subsections.heading: Explore and upgrade tools
paragraphs: Explore cards that open routes, create camp upgrades, or permanently improve cards support the official “modify forever” promise. A slightly weaker attack that you can grow repeatedly can beat a flashy one-off.

subsections.heading: Facility and gunk specialists
paragraphs: Official 0.6.39 notes clarify cleaning, over-cleaning into sparkle states, and many gunk-related cards. In Facility runs, cards that make gunk readable and controllable can be more valuable than generic Forgotten Path damage staples.

sections.heading: Mega Combo Ideas
paragraphs: Combo family 1: Draw into rage. Official Concerned Parent material shows temporary rage moods that grow whenever you draw, then convert a full hand of attacks into a huge payoff.
Combo family 2: Cook and eat. Official store copy pushes roasting, eating, and soup crafting. Draft combat cards that create food and explore or camp tools that upgrade food quality.
Combo family 3: Grow a starter forever. Official marketing repeatedly sells infinite modification. Keep a simple attack if camps and modify structures can push it beyond rare one-offs.

Combo family 4: Facility cleaning loops. Official patch notes discuss cleaning explanations, temporary Melty/Gunk Pile behavior, and related card edits. Build around understanding gunk rather than ignoring it.

sections.heading: Early Run vs Late Run Choices
paragraphs: Early: prefer reliable damage, any stable food source, and explore cards that prevent dead-end routing. Late: prefer multiplicative growth, recursive make-card effects, and tools that break a specific boss pattern.
Official patch 0.6.24 also noted that permanent food and data should keep Endless when permanently copied. That matters for late-run copying plans.

sections.heading: Version Caution and Named Patch Examples
paragraphs: Named examples from official patch notes include Acid Vial (fixed in 0.6.24) and many Facility cards adjusted in 0.6.39 such as Sweep, Gross Feast, Flash Turret, Analysis, and others. Those mentions are for version awareness, not automatic “pick these” recommendations.
This page will not publish a copied Fandom tier list or fabricated DPS table. If a card’s current numbers are not verified in the live client, we discuss the role instead.

faq.answer: It depends on character and pathway. Prioritize cards that support your deck role, scaling plan, and food or gunk systems rather than chasing a universal tier list.

faq.answer: Yes. Official patches such as 0.6.39 adjusted multiple cards and Facility behaviors. Always verify text in your build.

faq.question: Should I remove starter cards?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Official marketing highlights growing low-level starters into powerful attacks, so some starters are long-term engines.

faq.answer: Forgotten Path leans into the original fungal food and exploration fantasy. Facility adds its own pool and gunk/cleaning language. See the paths guide.

hero.heading: Shroom and Gloom Paths Guide
hero.lead: Early Access launches with two distinct Shroom and Gloom paths toward The Gloom. Forgotten Path is the established fungal route; Facility is the second pathway with its own cards, enemies, and systems. This guide compares them using official materials and patch-aware notes.

sections.heading: Path Overview
paragraphs: Official Early Access FAQ language says the current build offers two distinct pathways with unique characters and roughly 300 explore and combat cards per pathway. Official launch notes specifically celebrate The Mysterious Facility as a newly discoverable path with unique card pools, enemies, and rewards. Those two Shroom and Gloom paths are the only live routes covered here.
Developers also say a third pathway is planned during Early Access. This page only details the two live routes.

sections.heading: Forgotten Path
paragraphs: Forgotten Path is the route most trailer and diary content teaches first. It is also where public achievement Spelunker asks you to map every tunnel, so exploration completionists will spend serious time here.
Official patch 0.6.24 improved Forgotten Path by allowing more torches to spawn in more locations. If darkness and warmth pressure felt brutal at launch, update before judging the route.
Player-reported quest data also concentrates several early unlock objectives on Forgotten Path exploration and bosses. That makes the route valuable even after Facility unlocks.

sections.heading: Facility
paragraphs: Facility is officially positioned as a full second path, not a cosmetic palette swap. Launch notes promise unique cards, enemies, and rewards. Diary material previews gunk, machines, data, and Janitor-focused play.

Official patch 0.6.39 states that feedback and analytics showed Janitor and Facility were too challenging or complex for most new players, with only a small majority of runs ending in The Gloom. The patch aimed to make the playstyle easier to pick up without simply making Janitor outright stronger.
If you are new, unlock and sample Facility after you understand Forgotten Path basics. If you already like cleaning, resource conversion, and weird machine synergies, Facility is the deeper sandbox.

sections.heading: Which Path to Choose
bullets: Choose Forgotten Path to learn the double-deck loop and finish mapping achievements
Choose Forgotten Path while chasing player-reported character unlock exploration quests
Choose the Facility path after unlock when you want a separate card pool and gunk systems
Choose Facility with Janitor if you specifically want to master cleaning interactions
Switch paths when your quest log demands it rather than forcing one identity forever
paragraphs: Path choice depends on your goal, not on a universal ranking. There is no single best answer among the current Shroom and Gloom paths.
Official content density is split on purpose, with about 300 explore and combat cards per pathway according to the EA FAQ.

sections.heading: Risks, Rewards, and Patch Changes
paragraphs: Risk on Forgotten Path is often exploration completeness and resource pressure across many tunnels. Risk on Facility is system literacy: misreading gunk or cleaning can collapse a run even if your raw damage looks fine.

Reward on both paths is access to unique cards and encounters. Official EA plans also say future updates will add quests and challenges across all pathways, so investing in both routes remains useful.
Reviewed on 2026-09-17 against Steam store FAQ language and official patch notes for 0.6.24 and 0.6.39.

sections.heading: Path Choice by Player Goal
paragraphs: Goal: learn the game. Take Forgotten Path first. Official trailer and diary teaching, plus lower onboarding complexity, make it the safer classroom.
Goal: finish Spelunker or mapping quests. Stay on Forgotten Path until every tunnel is discovered. Switching early only delays those objectives.
Goal: see new card pools. Unlock and enter Facility after the pathway quest is complete. Official launch notes sell Facility as a full second pool, not a reskin.
Goal: practice Janitor systems. Use the Facility path after 0.6.39. Official notes focused that patch on making Facility and Janitor easier to understand for newer players.

sections.heading: Version Changes and Progress Checks
paragraphs: After a patch, re-check torch pressure on Forgotten Path and cleaning text on Facility before judging either route. Official 0.6.24 and 0.6.39 notes both touched path feel directly.

If a pathway still will not load, verify the unlock quest in your log and re-enter from the mode select screen after a client restart. Do not assume a missing path is a permanent account fault until those checks fail.
Keep achievements and quests in mind when planning path choice, but leave detailed card evaluation to the best cards page so this guide stays focused on route decisions.

faq.question: How many paths are in Shroom and Gloom right now?
faq.answer: Official Early Access materials describe two distinct pathways, with a third planned later during Early Access.

faq.question: What is the difference between Forgotten Path and Facility?
faq.answer: Forgotten Path is the core fungal route. Facility is a second pathway with its own card pool, enemies, and systems such as gunk and machines.

faq.question: Which path should beginners play?
faq.answer: Most new players should learn Forgotten Path first. Official 0.6.39 notes acknowledge Facility and Janitor were too challenging for many newcomers at launch.

faq.question: Did patches change the paths?
faq.answer: Yes. 0.6.24 improved Forgotten Path torch spawns. 0.6.39 focused on Facility and Janitor onboarding plus many related card behaviors.
